questions.question: Does the MLflow traces optimization work (RHAISTRAT-2250) require deliverables from the AI Core Platform team?

No — the component assignment was incorrect per the team lead

questions.question: What common hallucination pattern causes the pipeline to add GUI/UI requirements to infrastructure-only RFEs?
questions.expected_answer: The pipeline aggressively fills every template section even when the RFE is infrastructure-only. When Technical Approach and Affected Components sections need content, the agent infers dashboard or UI work that was never requested. This pattern was documented by mmortari across multiple STRATs — the agent added GUI requirements to RFEs that were purely about backend infrastructure, and proposed productizing upstream projects with no organizational mapping.
acceptable_variants: Agent injects UI work into infrastructure RFEs because it fills all template sections
Template completeness pressure causes the agent to hallucinate GUI requirements for infra-only work

questions.question: What conflation pattern caused the pipeline to hallucinate an 'MLflow AI Gateway UI' embedding requirement?
questions.expected_answer: The platform has prior art for embedding MLflow UI in the dashboard (RHAISTRAT-125, RHAISTRAT-150). When the agent processed an RFE about AI Gateway performance observability integration with MLflow (RHAIRFE-2625), it pattern-matched 'MLflow + Gateway' against this historical architecture context and produced a hallucinated requirement to embed a 'MLflow AI Gateway UI' that doesn't exist. The actual RFE was about observability and tracing, not UI embedding. The Razzmatazz team saw the STRAT and incorrectly assumed they had significant dashboard work coming.
acceptable_variants: Agent conflated historical MLflow UI embedding STRATs with an unrelated gateway observability RFE
Pattern-matching against RHAISTRAT-125/150 arch context produced a hallucinated UI embedding requirement for a tracing RFE
